newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria welcomes Commonwealth visit proposal.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria welcomes Commonwealth visit proposal.

text.p: Nigeria welcomes a Commonwealth decision to send a fact-finding mission, Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi was quoted on Tuesday as saying.

"We welcome their decision to come to Nigeria and attend a meeting between the Commonwealth and Nigeria and we look forward to the meeting," the News Agency of Nigeria quoted Ikimi as saying in New York.
Commonwealth ministers, meeting in New York, on Sunday decided to abandon talk of sanctions against Nigeria and said they would send a fact-finding mission instead.
They also scrapped an earlier insistence that any fact-finding group should be allowed to meet opposition groups and human rights campaigners.
"We believe that the difficulties we have with the Commonwealth can only be resolved through negotiations, discussion and dialogue," Ikimi said.

Nigeria was suspended from the 53-member group of Britain and its former colonies and protectorates last November after the execution of nine minority rights activists in the face of international appeals for clemency.
"Nigeria has not been standing still, a lot of changes have taken place in the country during the past year," Ikimi said.
The Commonwealth has said that military ruler General Sani Abacha's plan to return Nigeria to civilian rule by 1998 takes too long.
On Monday the electoral commission named the five political parties that will take part in the transition to democracy. Government opponents are not among them.
